notes.title: Steam Workshop is now available!
notes.content:
The game now supports Steam Workshops!

There are currently two main categories supported:

1. Data modification

You can modify or add class, items, skills, monsters and other data.

2. Picture modification

You can replace the main character group and most of the NPCs.


In addition, the bug that the character can't move in rare cases has been fixed.

notes.title: Major Update 「Mythic Epic」 Now Available
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

The first major update for The Nameless: Slay Dragon since its launch is now live! This update expands the game content by approximately 15% and comes with an 15% discounted sale. Additionally, a bundle with ASTLIBRA Revision is now available, offering even better value for players!

The Mythic Epic update was created in response to the enthusiastic feedback from players over the past few months. Its goal is to further enhance game mechanics, adjust combat balance, and expand content to cater to the diverse needs of players. 

Whether you're a new player or a veteran, seeking greater challenges or a more relaxed experience, the new version offers fresh fun and exciting experiences for everyone. Here are the specific updates:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44030634/ecbede11e209b36d02f8ee2f0707d90854b27515.png

New Class
 
Lancer
A fighter who fights with a long spear and can deal very powerful damage.
 
Heavy Warrior
Heavy weapons and armor, with the ability to count defense as part of your attack.
 
Pursuer
Hunts enemies for extra bounty and is good at creating extra weaknesses.
 
Spell Swordsman
Deals both magical and physical damage, and can sacrifice its own life to increase its attack power.
 
New Talent
 

 New Talent: Spear
 New talent: Heavy Weapon
 All talents can now be upgraded to SSS and have a special Power Spark!
 Spear now have the Spear talent upgraded!
 Axes and Great swords now have the Heavy Weapon talent upgraded!


Extra Game Mode
Dream Mode
-50% Enemy HP, -50% Enemy damage.

Easy Checks
+30% Success rate for all checks. 

Unlimited Rests
Time-limited bonuses available regardless of rest counts.

No Fatigue
No Fatigue accumulation.

Infinite Stock
Infinite stock in shops.

Limited Stock
Limited stock in shops.

Challenge Mode
Enemy power scales with number of defeated Bosses.

Mythic Epic Mode
Some enemies have a Mythic phase. Myht-level enemies may appear.

Mythic Epic mode includes new bosses, branches, and final chapter content.

Dragonslayer’s Burden
Enemy power scales with Dragonslaying Points (max at 500).

Unlimited Saves
Unlimited saves on max difficulty.

Main Character Traits
 
Fully Focused
 "Press Tab/LT up to three times a day
to boost success rate for exploration checks."

Infinite Potential
When Talent upgrades, selectable Potential Points increase from 3 to 4.

Natural Talent
+40% Talent growth rate in combat.

Master Craftsman
+15% Crafting success rate.

Master Trader
20% discount on shop items.

Inexhaustible Energy
20% reduction in Fatigue growth.

Unmatched Strength
Enhance Strength growth but reduce Intelligence growth.

Brilliant Mind
Enhance Intelligence growth but reduce Strength growth.

Dragonslayer Points Update

Extra Trait
All characters gain an additional Talent slot.

Extra Accessory
All characters gain an additional Accessory slot.

Peak Start
Inherit all Talent levels from the previous playthrough.

 
Other

 Added a few map events and dialogs
 Added new bosses and monsters
 Added an unimportant ending in Mythic Epic mode
 Added a new CG image
 Lovely Witch Staff can now be upgraded to Super Lovely Witch Staff
 Added a rune that can be used to select Aeons to awaken.


This update aims to increase the game's playability and provide more playable modes, so hopefully both light, hardcore, and episodic players will find something enjoyable ^^

notes.title: The Nameless: Slay Dragon to Receive a Major Update in January 2025
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It has been over two months since the release of The Nameless: Slay Dragon, and we are thrilled by the overwhelming support and love from players. With nearly a thousand reviews, the game has earned a "Very Positive" rating!

Major Update Coming in January 2025
Since the release, we have been paying close attention to player feedback and have made frequent updates, mostly in the form of small patches. Now, after two months of gathering feedback and with the developers' continued efforts, The Nameless: Slay Dragon is finally set to receive its first major update in January 2025!

Whether you're still searching for the most effective skill combinations or have lamented over a particular ending, this update will have a significant impact on your gaming experience. What changes will take place in this world? What new possibilities await our story? Which setting will become more reasonable? Which enemies will we fear more? Stay tuned for more details!

Join the Autumn Sale
To celebrate this major update and introduce more players to this unique and captivating fantasy world, The Nameless: Slay Dragon will also be part of the upcoming Steam Autumn Sale. If you've been on the fence, now is the time to take a look – don't miss out!

Official Soundtrack Release
Music is a key part of the game's experience, and the developers have invited artist Larse to create a series of beautiful compositions for The Nameless: Slay Dragon. The official soundtrack is now available for purchase, so let the adventurous melodies accompany your everyday life!

Steam Awards Voting
If you've enjoyed The Nameless: Slay Dragon, we kindly ask you to consider voting for it in the Steam Awards under the "Outstanding Story-Rich Game" category. Your support is our greatest motivation!

Have Fun!

notes.title: Steam Next Fest & Devblog
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

The Nameless: Slay Dragon is now participating Steam Next Fest. You are welcome to play the demo and give us your feedback! Thank you very much!

In the meantime, another devblog:
I believe that the secret to developing a good game lies in identifying the essential pleasures it provides.
As an RPG enthusiast, I've asked myself: what is the core joy of RPGs?
Here are the answers I've come up with:

1. Gaining unique life experiences through the story

In my view, RPGs can be likened to a living being where the art and sound are the skin, the gameplay is the bones and flesh, and the story is the soul. Why should we care about the story of a game? Because it provides life-like experiences without the stakes: you can go on adventures without truly leaving your loved ones, fight battles without physical danger, and forge deep bonds without actual social interaction. Although these experiences aren't real, they enrich us with unforgettable memories. Like I mentioned earlier, the story is the soul of an RPG.

2. Receiving constant feedback

The largest difference between games and the real world lies in the fact that games consistently offer instant and positive feedback, which is seldom the case in reality. In RPGs, positive feedback is manifested through character development, acquiring experience and abilities, and improving skills and knowledge. Not all feedback has to be positive—as the frustration from challenging levels can attest. Such feedback offers motivation and the courage to defeat hardships, followed by the sense of accomplishment that comes with victory.

3. Having the power to control something

We don't get to choose our looks or origins in the real world, but in a game, you can decide the fate of the world or even the universe. If you play by the rules, your moves will yield the outcomes you intend. The world of gaming grants you a form of omnipotence, allowing you to reshape the fate of its universe time and again, until it aligns with your vision. This is why we always expect a high degree of freedom to make choices in RPGs.

4. The process of self-discovery

RPG stands for role-playing game; playing a role isn't about becoming that entity, but exploring our potential—who we can become, what we hope to see, the choices we might make, and the life we want to lead. A good RPG may not always provide answers, but it will always pose questions.

All these essential pleasures stem from a single word: fantasy. To fulfill these fantasies, humans have dedicated countless hours, building sophisticated and wondrous worlds, which in turn has shaped our society and civilization.

From a game design perspective, making a good RPG involves:

1. Telling a memorable story
2. Balancing positive feedback with game complexity and challenges
3. Providing extensive freedom and customization options
4. Detailing a rich world and character relationships that players can relate to
5. Completing and releasing the game

Applying these criteria to 'The Nameless: Slay Dragon', I'd say I've achieved 1 and 2. As for player freedom, my current budget doesn't allow for character customization or an extensive range of dialogue options. However, with over 20 classes and several endings, I'd say the level of freedom is just about acceptable.

As for the fourth point, the construction of the game's universe is fairly solid, and I'm currently writing the side stories of characters, hoping for good results.

Lastly, my wish is for the game to be brought to completion successfully!

notes.title: Dev Blog & Happy Holidays
notes.content:
Hi guys,

Through our participation in Chengdu G-Fusion Showcase and the on-site playtesting, I identified several issues that need to be addressed. Specifically, poor guidance in the game has resulted confusion among players regarding the game mechanics.

Therefore, I have decided to adjust the guidance accordingly.


 SOULFORCE – The introduction of Soulforce was originally planned for a later stage in the game, but I have decided to put a brief introduction during the first combat instead.
 ENEMY INTENTS – Previously in the HELP tab, it will now be prompted during the first encounter with a mini Boss.
 ENEMY IAKNESS - Previously in the HELP tab, it will now be prompted during the first encounter with a mini Boss.
 CHARACTER SWITCHING – While the game does enable the switching of character actions, there is currently no tutorial on it. I will include one.
 ACCESSIBILITY – Movement controls require improvement. I are currently enhancing the pull and range of the event nodes, but this could potentially result in bugs that I are addressing individually.
 PUZZLE – Upon three failed attempts on certain puzzles, hints will be prompted to prevent players from getting stuck.
 More autosave checkpoints will be added to prevent significant progress loss after a GAMEOVER.
 I are in the final stages of proofreading for the English translations and will soon update an improved multilingual version.
 Currently in the process of producing the trailer. Video editing proves to be quite challenging for a solo developer.
 The UI modifications are still pending, and I am actively seeking assistance in redesigning the UI icons.
 The narrative performance and BOSS AI require significant adjustments.
 During the following months, there will be a considerable workload, and I will take things step by step.


I wish you all happy holidays!
